title: ID. POLO & ID.3 Neo – Transfer and De-tagging Guidance
body:
### ID. POLO and ID.3 Neo with SOC in the options

Vehicles with the SOC option code must not be transferred, regardless of whether the vehicle is an ID. POLO or an ID.3 Neo.

**Transfers:** Do not action any transfer requests for vehicles with SOC in the options.

**ID. POLO de-tagging:** Do not de-tag.

**ID.3 Neo de-tagging:** De-tagging is permitted, as demo requirements have not been prescribed in the same way as for ID. POLO.

**What to do if a transfer is requested:**

* Decline the transfer request.
* Refer the retailer to the Believe in BEV Guide to check the relevant standards.
* If the retailer still wishes to discuss the transfer, refer them to the brand inbox for further review.

### ID. POLO without SOC but with a block

If an ID. POLO does not have the SOC option code but has a block on the vehicle, the following actions are permitted:

* **Transfers:** Permitted.
* **De-tagging:** Permitted.
* **Removing blocks:** Not permitted under any circumstances.

**Important:** The block must remain in place to prevent retailers from registering vehicles early.

### Temporary arrangement

This guidance is temporary and applies until the ID. POLO launch weekend, 6–8 November.

After the launch weekend:

* Retailers should have registered the vehicles required to meet the standards.
* The brand's auditing process will identify any issues with compliance.

### Quick reference

* **ID. POLO with SOC:** Do not transfer. Do not de-tag. Do not remove a block.
* **ID.3 Neo with SOC:** Do not transfer. De-tagging is permitted. Do not remove a block.
* **ID. POLO without SOC but with a block:** Transfers and de-tagging are permitted. Removing the block is not permitted.

**Key rule:** If SOC is present, decline all transfer requests and refer the retailer to the Believe in BEV Guide. Any further discussion about transfers must be directed to the brand inbox.
